headline: EC suspends 'Boat' symbol and finalizes 120 election symbols
summary: The Election Commission has updated its list of available symbols for the upcoming national election, removing the 'Boat' from active allocation.
details: The Election Commission (EC) has finalized a list of 120 electoral symbols for candidates in the upcoming national election.
A key change in the updated list is the suspension of the 'Boat' symbol, which is now marked as 'suspended' in the official registry.
The EC issued a notification on September 15, amending the Election Conduct Rules, 2008, under the powers granted by the Representation of the People Order, 1972.
According to the revised rules, symbols can be allocated to candidates from the available list, excluding those that have been suspended under specific clauses.
The final list of 120 symbols includes a wide variety of items such as the pineapple, apple, mango, eagle, camel, computer, pen, sickle, and others.
It also introduces a 'No' option for solo candidates, allowing voters to express their lack of preference for any candidate.
The notification was signed by Election Commissioner and Senior Secretary Akhtar Ahmed, and all future electoral activities will follow these revised guidelines.
caption:
The 'Boat' is out. The Election Commission has finalized 120 symbols for the next national election, but one major one is suspended.

The Election Commission (EC) has finalized a list of 120 electoral symbols for candidates in the upcoming national election.

A key change in the updated list is the suspension of the 'Boat' symbol, which is now marked as 'suspended' in the official registry.

The EC issued a notification on September 15, amending the Election Conduct Rules, 2008, under the powers granted by the Representation of the People Order, 1972.

According to the revised rules, symbols can be allocated to candidates from the available list, excluding those that have been suspended under specific clauses.

The final list of 120 symbols includes a wide variety of items such as the pineapple, apple, mango, eagle, camel, computer, pen, sickle, and others.

It also introduces a 'No' option for solo candidates, allowing voters to express their lack of preference for any candidate.

The notification was signed by Election Commissioner and Senior Secretary Akhtar Ahmed, and all future electoral activities will follow these revised guidelines.

headline_marked: PM Tareke Rahman [[wishes Narendra Modi happy birthday]]
headline: PM Tareke Rahman wishes Narendra Modi happy birthday
summary: Indian PM Narendra Modi thanked the Bangladeshi PM for his heartfelt wishes on his 76th birthday.
details: Prime Minister Tareke Rahman wished Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi a happy birthday on X (formerly Twitter) on Thursday night.
In his post, PM Tareke Rahman expressed his best wishes for Modi's health and happiness, praising his dedicated service to the people of India.
The Prime Minister's Office of Bangladesh also shared a greeting card featuring Narendra Modi's photo on Facebook to convey the same message.
Within half an hour of the post, Narendra Modi responded on X, sharing Tareke Rahman's post and thanking him for the heartfelt wishes.
Modi wrote, 'Thank you Prime Minister Tareke Rahman for your heartfelt wishes. I deeply appreciate your kind words.'
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi celebrated his 76th birthday on Thursday, September 17.
caption:
A warm exchange between leaders: PM Tareke Rahman wishes Narendra Modi a happy birthday, and Modi responds with gratitude.

Prime Minister Tareke Rahman wished Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi a happy birthday on X (formerly Twitter) on Thursday night.

In his post, PM Tareke Rahman expressed his best wishes for Modi's health and happiness, praising his dedicated service to the people of India.

The Prime Minister's Office of Bangladesh also shared a greeting card featuring Narendra Modi's photo on Facebook to convey the same message.

Within half an hour of the post, Narendra Modi responded on X, sharing Tareke Rahman's post and thanking him for the heartfelt wishes.

Modi wrote, 'Thank you Prime Minister Tareke Rahman for your heartfelt wishes. I deeply appreciate your kind words.'

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi celebrated his 76th birthday on Thursday, September 17.
